title: Sell Mineral Rights in Wilburn, AR
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Wilburn, AR | Cleburne County
metaDescription: Wilburn sits in Cleburne County, one of the original core Fayetteville Shale counties. We price your mineral interest off actual well production and title.
heroLead: Wilburn is a small unincorporated community in Cleburne County, one of the four original core counties where the Fayetteville Shale was drilled hardest.
intro: Cleburne County, and the rural land around Wilburn in particular, sat inside the dense horizontal drilling program SEECO and other operators ran through the mid-2000s and into the 2010s. Between that and the county's better-known geography around Greers Ferry Lake, a lot of families here own small mineral tracts on land that's stayed in the same hands for generations, land that was never subdivided or sold off, just leased and pooled when the shale boom came through.

sections.heading: Core-County Density Around Wilburn
paragraphs: Because Cleburne County was core Fayetteville Shale acreage, tracts near Wilburn are more likely than flank-county land to be pooled into a producing unit with multiple wells. That production history is the main thing we price against, checked directly against Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission records rather than assumed from the county's reputation.

sections.heading: Small, Rural, and Often Undivided
paragraphs: A lot of Wilburn-area interests are small by acreage but haven't been formally split among heirs, which can leave a division order out of date. We confirm current ownership through the Cleburne County Circuit Clerk's records in Heber Springs before putting a number on the table.

faqs.question: Is my royalty check from land near Wilburn too small to be worth selling?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Even a modest ongoing check can add up to a meaningful lump sum when priced against the well's remaining production, and there's no minimum size we require to make an offer.

faqs.question: How do I know which well my Wilburn tract is pooled with?
faqs.answer: Your division order or a recent royalty statement usually names the well and unit. If you don't have either, we can research it through Cleburne County records and the Arkansas Oil and Gas Commission.

faqs.question: Our family land has never been formally divided among the heirs. Can you still buy it?
faqs.answer: Yes, though we'll need to confirm the heirship first, typically through a probate file or affidavit, before we can close on any one heir's share.

faqs.question: What makes Cleburne County different from a flank county like White?
faqs.answer: Cleburne was one of the four original core counties, so well density and production history here tend to run higher than in counties the play only reached during its later expansion.

faqs.question: How fast can you close on a small Wilburn-area interest?
faqs.answer: A clean, single-owner tract usually closes within a few weeks once we've confirmed title. Undivided family land takes a bit longer while we sort out heirship documentation.
